requirements.title: One advanced or applied AI course
Exclusive minor credits
requirements.summary: At least 12 credits must be discrete to this minor.

requirements.title: Minor residence and overlap
requirements.summary: Complete 12 semester credits at Lewis & Clark and 12 exclusive to this minor; the exclusive credits cannot satisfy another major or minor.

requirements.title: Minor GPA
requirements.summary: Maintain a minor GPA of at least 2.000.

requirements.title: Declaration and certification
requirements.summary: Declare with the registrar; the chair certifies completion on the degree application. At most two minors appear on the transcript.

requirements.title: Approved credit shortage
requirements.summary: The registrar may waive a one-credit shortage arising from the specified advanced-standing, overseas or approved transfer-credit circumstances. Other shortages require petition approval.

requirements.title: Credit/no-credit and repeated courses
requirements.summary: CR/NC election in regularly graded courses requires instructor consent and timely filing; it is excluded from GPA. Repeating a nonrepeatable course does not earn credit twice; both grades enter GPA.

requirements.title: Transfer approval
requirements.summary: Transfer courses require registrar eligibility review and chair/program-director approval for minor applicability; grades must meet the C− threshold.

requirements.title: Transfer CR/NC evidence
requirements.summary: Transferred pass/no-pass or credit/no-credit courses require the awarding institution to document a passing standard of C− or higher.

notes: Complete review covers this minor’s local curriculum and applicable College of Arts and Sciences minor policies; it does not certify the parent BA degree.
The single published advanced/applied option is CS469; the parser preserves the source’s choose-one group.
All fifteen named courses now have independently reviewed semester-credit amounts; 24 is the published minor minimum, not a computed elective-pool sum.
First-offered date is unknown. The overview calls this a new program but gives no launch date.
General CR/NC policy is recorded without inventing a minor-specific ban. Transfer applicability requires individual chair/program-director approval.

All ten non-CS options now have concise catalog descriptions, prerequisites and explicit semester-credit amounts from the Economics, Mathematics, Psychology, Philosophy and Communication catalogs. Source-stated None prerequisites are recorded only where explicit; class-standing restrictions remain attached. ECON 303 prerequisite punctuation is retained without imposing an invented logical grouping. All fifteen named courses have descriptions, prerequisites and credits; public course sites/syllabi and a first-offered date remain unverified. The overview calls the minor new without dating its first offering.
